title: Streaky lines on printouts
symptom: Printouts have dark lines or streaks running down the page
user_description: Every page I print has ugly streaks running down it. It's a contract for a client, so I can't send this.

options.why: A driver cannot make physical streaks. It should be ruled out only after checking whether the printer itself is at fault.

options.text: Print the printer's own test page. If the streaks appear there, run its cleaning routine and check the toner and drum as the manual advises
options.why: A test page printed by the printer itself separates a printer fault from a document or driver problem. Streaks on it point to dirty or worn parts such as toner or drum.
Paper size does not cause streaks. This changes something unrelated to the fault.
Pointless. The streaks appear on paper, so the PC is not the cause.

hints: How can you tell whether the printer or the document is causing the streaks?
Which parts inside a laser printer touch the paper and can get dirty or worn?
Where would you find the correct cleaning steps?
real_world_tip: Check whether the streaks are in the same place on every page. A fixed streak usually points to a worn or dirty part.
